fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Front Driveway; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Long Driveway; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate the turn-in during low-visibility or nighttime conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Maintain a minimum vertical clearance along the driveway to allow fire apparatus and ambulances to pass without branches contacting the vehicle.
• Clear a turnaround area near the residence large enough for a fire engine or ambulance to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Mark or communicate the turnaround location to arriving units so drivers do not commit to a dead end without a planned exit.
• Keep the area around the detached structure clear of dense vegetation so responders can reach and move around it without obstruction.
• Confirm that perimeter fencing has at least one gate accessible from the driveway and that the gate can be opened quickly without a key or combination.
• Keep that gate unlocked or secured with a combination known to local fire and EMS, or install a Knox-compatible lock.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of the main residence, detached structure, and any gates, so arriving responders can

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Open Green Space; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access; Grass Cover; Brush Area; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between tree canopies and the roofline.
• Cut and remove brush in the area immediately surrounding the structure.
• Mow or cut grass cover close to the structure during dry periods when grass cures and dries out.
• Clear any dead or dry plant material from the ground near the base of the structure.
• Remove low-hanging tree branches that extend over the roof or near exterior walls.
• Thin mixed vegetation on the sides of the single access route to keep the travel lane clear for vehicles.
• Keep the full width of the driveway free of overhanging branches to allow emergency vehicle passage.
• Cut back brush and tall grass along the limited rear access path to maintain a clear route around the structure.
• Separate any wood piles, outdoor furniture, or stored materials from the exterior walls of the structure.
• Keep the open green space areas adjacent to the structure mowed short and free of accumulated dead grass or leaves.
